# Story 27 — View full ticket history

## Prerequisites

- Story 11 (**update ticket status**) completed — introduced `statusHistory` on `Ticket.ts`. This story reads that field; it does **not** introduce a new parallel history mechanism.
- Story 10 (**auto-assign a ticket**) / Story 15 (**manually reassign a ticket**) and Story 8/11 (**categorize/prioritize**) reviewed: at the time of writing there is **no** `assignmentHistory` or `categoryHistory` sub-document on `Ticket.ts` (`backend/src/models/Ticket.ts` lines 23–45 lists only `statusHistory` beyond current-state fields). The composed timeline in this story therefore covers **status changes, replies, and internal notes** exactly, plus **escalation** (which is already a status change to `"escalated"` in `statusHistory`). Category / assignment change entries are an **explicit gap** carried by this story into `## Edge Cases & Failure Modes` — do **not** fabricate placeholder entries; add a `TODO(story-future)` comment where a future audit-log integration point will live.
- Coordination note for whoever plans a "reassignment audit log" or "category audit log" later: the aggregator function this story adds must be the single place they wire new entry sources into.
- Story 26 (**in-app notifications for ticket events**, `.squad/plans/ticket-management/26-story-in-app-notifications-for-ticket-events.md`) reviewed for terminology parity — event kinds surfaced in notifications should map 1:1 to `kind` strings emitted by this story's history endpoint.

---

## Story Goal

Give an authenticated staff user viewing a ticket a **single chronological timeline** of everything meaningful that has happened on that ticket:

1. **Ticket created** (from `Ticket.createdAt` + `Ticket.customer`).
2. **Status changed** — one entry per element of `Ticket.statusHistory`, including the `"escalated"` transition (which also carries `escalatedTo`).
3. **Reply posted** — one entry per `Message` where `parentType: "ticket"` and `internal !== true`.
4. **Internal note added** — one entry per `Message` where `parentType: "ticket"` and `internal === true`.

Two consumption surfaces per the approved mockup:

- **Compact "Recent activity"** teaser in the agent sidebar (last 5 events, chronological desc), with a "View full history" affordance that reveals the full timeline inline.
- **Full timeline + "Export history" button** in the sub-admin sidebar; the export button is gated by a new `tickets:export_history` permission key.

**Export interpretation (explicitly chosen):** the export endpoint returns the same aggregated history payload as JSON with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="ticket-<ticketNumber>-history.json"`. A formatted CSV / PDF pipeline is **out of scope** and noted as a follow-up.

**Not in scope:**
- Any mutation of ticket status / category / assignment (Stories 8–12, 15).
- Adding `categoryHistory` / `assignmentHistory` sub-documents (belongs to whichever future story wires audit logs into those mutations).
- A dedicated "history page" URL — the timeline lives inside the existing ticket-detail view.

## Product rules (from story)

- **History is read-only** for every persona. No route or UI in this story mutates a ticket.
- **Regular agents** see the compact "Recent activity" teaser + inline expand to full timeline, but **no export button**.
- **Sub-admins (and any account granted `tickets:export_history`)** see the same full timeline plus an "Export history" button.
- **Customers do not see this history.** Customer-facing ticket-status is Story 40 (`customer-portal/track-ticket-status-from-the-portal`) and is not extended here.

### 2 — Add a history aggregator service

**Create file:** `backend/src/services/ticketHistory.service.ts`

Define and export:

```ts
export type TicketHistoryEventKind =
  | "created"
  | "status_changed"
  | "reply_posted"
  | "internal_note_added";

export interface TicketHistoryEvent {
  kind: TicketHistoryEventKind;
  at: Date;
  actor: { id: string; name: string | null; role: string } | null;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export async function buildTicketHistory(ticketId: Types.ObjectId): Promise<TicketHistoryEvent[]>;
```

Behaviour:

- Load the `Ticket` (fail with a typed "not found" error if missing).
- Emit a single `"created"` event from `ticket.createdAt` with `actor` = the customer (populate `User.name` / `role`), and `data: { ticketNumber, subject }`.
- Emit one `"status_changed"` event per `statusHistory` entry, populated with the `changedBy` user. `data: { to: entry.status }` (and `escalatedTo` if the current `ticket.escalatedTo` is set **and** this is the last `escalated` transition — do not fabricate a per-entry escalation target since `statusHistory` doesn't store it).
- Query `Message.find({ parentType: "ticket", parentId: ticketId }).sort({ createdAt: 1 }).populate("senderId", "name role")` — the compound index at `Message.ts` covers this. Split into `reply_posted` vs. `internal_note_added` on `message.internal`.
- Merge all events, sort **ascending** by `at`, and return.
- **Do not** include the raw message body in `data` for `internal_note_added` when caller passes `{ redactInternalBodies: true }` — reserve this option flag but default to `false`; document why (future customer-portal reuse).

Add a `TODO(story-future)` comment inside the file listing the two missing event kinds (`category_changed`, `assignee_changed`) with a pointer back to Story 15 and Story 8 so a future audit-log story wires them in exactly one place.

### 3 — Wire the two GET endpoints

**File:** `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts`

- Import `buildTicketHistory` and (for the export) the new permission key.
- Register `GET /:id/history`:
  - `requireAuth`.
  - Load the ticket; enforce the **same** visibility gate already used by the existing single-ticket GET route (customer sees only their own, agent needs to be `assignedAgent` **or** have `tickets:view_all`, sub-admin sees all). Copy the check verbatim from the existing single-ticket handler in this file — do not reimplement.
  - Return `{ ticketId, events: TicketHistoryEvent[] }` as JSON.
- Register `GET /:id/history/export`:
  - `requireAuth` + `requirePermission("tickets:export_history")`.
  - Same visibility gate (defence in depth — the permission alone is not a bypass).
  - Set headers: `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="ticket-<ticketNumber>-history.json"`.
  - Body: `JSON.stringify({ ticket: { id, ticketNumber, subject, status, customer, assignedAgent, category, priority, createdAt }, events }, null, 2)`.

Both routes must live **above** any wildcard `/:id` matcher to avoid collisions — mirror the ordering already used for other nested ticket sub-routes in this file.

Add a one-line comment above each new route pointing to `.squad/plans/ticket-management/27-story-view-full-ticket-history.md`.

### 4 — No new model changes

Explicitly: **do not** add `categoryHistory`, `assignmentHistory`, or a `TicketEvent` collection in this story. That is what Story 15 (or a dedicated audit-log story) is for. Aggregation reads existing fields only.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Ticket has zero non-creation events.** Expected: sidebar shows the single `Ticket created` row and the "View full history" toggle stays visible but expands to the same single row; export still works. Enforced in `TicketDetailSidebar.tsx` (`events.length === 1` render branch).
- **`statusHistory` empty on an old ticket.** Old tickets predating Story 11 will have `statusHistory: []`. Expected: only `created` + message events show, no synthetic entries. Enforced by the aggregator naturally.
- **Message with a deleted sender.** `populate("senderId", ...)` returns `null`. Expected: `actor: null`; UI shows a fallback label ("Unknown user"). Enforced in `ticketHistoryService.buildTicketHistory` and the sidebar row.
- **Category or assignee changed but no history exists.** Explicit gap: the current-value fields still show in the ticket header; the timeline has no entry. `TODO(story-future)` comment in `ticketHistory.service.ts` documents this; **do not** invent a "category changed" event from `updatedAt`.
- **Customer trying to hit `GET /:id/history` for their own ticket.** Reuses the existing single-ticket visibility gate, so a customer sees their own; **however**, message rows with `internal: true` must be filtered out before returning. The aggregator accepts a `viewerRole` parameter and skips internal notes when `viewerRole === "customer"`. Enforced in `ticketHistory.service.ts`.
- **Regular agent hits `GET /:id/history/export` directly.** `requirePermission("tickets:export_history")` rejects with 403; the frontend never rendered the button, so this is a defence-in-depth check only.
- **Very long history (hundreds of events).** No pagination for now — the timeline is expected to fit; ticket volumes at this scale don't exist yet. Add a `// pagination TODO` comment in the route handler with a suggested query-param shape (`?before=<isoDate>&limit=<n>`) so a future story picks it up cleanly.
- **Concurrent status change while the sidebar is open.** Not addressed in this story — the sidebar is a snapshot at page load. Any real-time refresh belongs with Story 26 (notifications).
- **Non-JSON exports.** Explicitly not supported. If the request has `Accept: text/csv`, still return JSON; the endpoint does not content-negotiate.

5. **Manual — agent persona:** log in as an agent assigned to a ticket that has ≥ 3 status changes and ≥ 1 internal note; open the ticket detail; confirm the "Recent activity" section shows 5 rows and the "View full history" toggle expands the full timeline. Confirm **no** "Export history" button.
6. **Manual — sub-admin persona:** log in as a sub-admin; open the same ticket; confirm the timeline renders and the "Export history" anchor downloads `ticket-<ticketNumber>-history.json` with a valid JSON body.
7. **Manual — customer persona:** log in as the customer who owns the ticket; open the customer-portal ticket view (Story 40 view). Confirm no internal note text appears in any surface (this story doesn't add a customer-visible timeline, but the backend endpoint must not leak internal notes if hit — verify with a direct `curl` using the customer's session cookie).
8. **Regression:** in `backend/`, run `npm test -- ticket.routes` and confirm the pre-existing status-change tests around lines 1100 / 1254 / 1511 still pass unchanged.
9. **Regression — permission enumeration:** in `backend/`, run `npm test -- constants/permissions`.
